title: ASENA narcotics analysis software flags a car at the Köy Hizmetleri checkpoint in Şırnak; the dog Hector finds 86.6 kg of skunk in 119 packages and three lawyers are remanded
summary: Şırnak police stopped a car selected by the ASENA narcotics analysis software; the dog Hector found 86.6 kg of skunk in 119 packages in the trunk, and three lawyers were remanded (March 2025).
account: In May 2022 Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said that ASENA starts following people who go to a province, take a route or stay at a hotel for the first time. He claimed that it had helped solve 3,593 cases. In March 2025 Şırnak Provincial Police stopped a vehicle at the Köy Hizmetleri (Village Services) police checkpoint after ASENA selected it for inspection. DHA calls ASENA police software “in artificial intelligence format”. The narcotics dog Hector then found 86 kilograms 600 grams of skunk in 119 packages hidden in the trunk. Three occupants, M.E., H.K. and Ş.A., were detained (Sözcü/DHA and Habertürk/DHA, 17 March 2025). Diken, citing İHA, gives ASENA's full name as Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı (Narcotics Analysis Systems Network). It says that the three were lawyers registered with the Mardin Bar Association. They were taken to court after police processing and remanded in custody (Diken, 18 March 2025). None of the reports gives the day of the stop, what data ASENA analyzed or how it chose the car, or any official's name. No later report gives the outcome of the case against the three lawyers after the remand that Diken reported on 18 March 2025.
purpose: Police analysis software built to pick out vehicles and people likely to be carrying narcotics for checkpoint stops. This seizure was that use.
system: ASENA (Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı), Turkish police narcotics analysis software
deployer: Şırnak Provincial Police Directorate (Turkish National Police)

ratings.reason: 86.6 kg of skunk was taken out of circulation and three suspects were remanded, per the DHA and İHA reports. No report shows a harm that was about to occur, so the public benefit is the seizure itself.
The Şırnak police turned a software flag into a large seizure and three remands, per the DHA and İHA reports. A measurable result for the unit.

ai_role.statement: ASENA picked the car, and the dog Hector and the officers found the drugs and made the arrests. In 2022 the Interior Minister declined to give details of how ASENA works. He said that it starts following a person who goes to a province, uses a route or stays at a hotel for the first time, by comparing various data. No source describes what ASENA flagged in this stop or whether an analyst reviewed the flag before it.

fields.summary: Şırnak police stopped a car selected by the ASENA narcotics analysis software; the dog Hector found 86.6 kg of skunk in 119 packages in the trunk, and three lawyers were remanded (March 2025).
fields.account: In May 2022 Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said that ASENA starts following people who go to a province, take a route or stay at a hotel for the first time. He claimed that it had helped solve 3,593 cases. In March 2025 Şırnak Provincial Police stopped a vehicle at the Köy Hizmetleri (Village Services) police checkpoint after ASENA selected it for inspection. DHA calls ASENA police software “in artificial intelligence format”. The narcotics dog Hector then found 86 kilograms 600 grams of skunk in 119 packages hidden in the trunk. Three occupants, M.E., H.K. and Ş.A., were detained (Sözcü/DHA and Habertürk/DHA, 17 March 2025). Diken, citing İHA, gives ASENA's full name as Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı (Narcotics Analysis Systems Network). It says that the three were lawyers registered with the Mardin Bar Association. They were taken to court after police processing and remanded in custody (Diken, 18 March 2025). None of the reports gives the day of the stop, what data ASENA analyzed or how it chose the car, or any official's name. No later report gives the outcome of the case against the three lawyers after the remand that Diken reported on 18 March 2025.
